sections.h2: Jeff Davis County at a glance
sections.html:
Jeff Davis County is farm and timber country in southeast Georgia. Hazlehurst, the biggest town, holds the county seat, and Denton is the one other incorporated city. The county has an estimated 15,219 residents as of July 2025, up 3.0% from the 2020 count of 14,779.

Prices run low. For 2020-2024 the middle value of an owned home is $118,300, and owners live in 71.3% of the homes. County builders took out just nine permits in 2025, which leaves resales with little new competition. You will mostly be up against other older houses, and your likely buyer is a local who knows the area. A Hazlehurst house, a rural place by a crossroads and a cut-over timber tract each draw a different crowd, so judge each against its own comparable sales.

sections.h2: Who to call about Jeff Davis County property tax
sections.html:
Start at the Tax Commissioner, 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, Hazlehurst, GA 31539, telephone (912) 375-6622. Letters go to PO Box 558, and the counter closes at 4:30 on weekdays. You can also pay through an online portal. Close to a deadline, ask the staff how to pay so the check does not arrive late.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends and collects bills, hands out mobile home decals, and also takes timber, heavy duty equipment and intangible tax
  • Tax Assessor, (912) 375-6624: sets values and receives appeals
  • Board of Equalization: the Grand Jury names its members to rule on value disputes
  • County commissioners and the school board: choose the millage rates

Have the parcel number or owner's name ready when you call, plus the mailing address you want bills sent to. The commissioner does not set your house's value or the millage rate, so a value complaint belongs with the assessor.

Bills usually go out October 20 and come due December 20, and you may pay in pieces before then. Once that date passes, interest accrues each month at the bank prime rate, and a further 5% penalty lands every 120 days until the total reaches 20%. A balance left for a year grows noticeably, and any payoff quote goes stale fast.

  • Mobile homes are billed in January and due April 1, and a decal goes on the home once you pay
  • After April 1 the home picks up a 10% filing penalty and 1% a month, then a FiFa on the clerk's docket and possible auction
  • If you own the land under a mobile home, it can be homesteaded and is taxed as real property

Mobile home dates vary from one county page to another, so phone the Tax Commissioner for yours before counting on April 1.

The base exemption deducts two thousand dollars from assessed value. It reduces county and school tax, and does not touch municipal school levies or bond debt.

The application window runs January 1 to April 1, and you file at the Tax Commissioner's counter between 8 and 5 on weekdays. Georgia law allows no extension, so if you miss April 1 you go without the exemption that year. After approval it renews on its own until your situation changes, and it can never exceed the tax owed.

Three other programs cover land and buildings:

  • Conservation use, including residential transitional land
  • Agricultural preferential assessment
  • Rehabilitated historic property

Every one of them binds the owner, by covenant with the Tax Assessor, to keep the qualifying use going for ten years or longer. Thinking of selling enrolled land? Call (912) 375-6624 and ask what a new owner would have to honor.

Your appeal is a letter to the Board of Tax Assessors, sent within 45 days of the notice, and it should say which appeal route you want. Spring is when notices for real and personal property normally arrive.

The county hears four complaints: the parcel is not taxable, the value is wrong, it is assessed out of step with similar parcels, or an exemption was refused. Complaining about the millage rate or the size of the bill is not a ground. If you file a return during the January 1 to April 1 window and give your own opinion of the January 1 market value, your appeal rights survive a later change to the figure. Mobile home owners get 45 days from the bill mailing, then 21 days after a notice of change, to reach the Board of Equalization.

Taxable property gets reported to the Tax Assessors Office between January 1 and April 1. Skip the filing and the prior year's value and real property exemptions simply continue.

Appraisers study recent sales and conditions as of January 1, and the spring notice shows what the county thinks each parcel is worth. Read it the day it arrives. The 45-day appeal clock starts on the notice date, not on the day you open the envelope.

  • Report a new mailing address fast, because notices go to the last address on file
  • Approved exemptions renew yearly until eligibility changes

Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff, and let the closing office pay it from your sale proceeds. Interest runs monthly and penalties step up every 120 days, so an old quote may come up short. Request the number near closing, and again if the date slips into another month.

The order is simple: get the payoff, have the closing office pay it, and keep the receipt. A FiFa on the clerk's docket is public record. Any title search finds it, so it has to be cleared before the deed passes.

Timber land may owe timber tax, billed by the same office. If your mobile home sits on rented ground, confirm the decal and the April 1 bill before listing. A cash buyer skips lender appraisals and repair haggling, though the payoff, title search and recorded deed all still happen.

sections.h2: Refunds, city tax and recording tax
sections.html:
Tax assessed or collected by mistake, or illegally, can be refunded. Ask in writing, no later than three years after you paid. If an appeal lowers your value, the refund follows once the final taxable value is set.

Both Hazlehurst and Denton may levy a city property tax, and the city clerk usually sends that bill unless city and county agreed on a single combined one. Vehicle tax is collected only by the county Tax Commissioner. Voters can also approve a freeport exemption for commercial and industrial inventory, applied for in the same window as returns.

If you buy or finance land, a long-term note secured by the property must be recorded within 90 days. The state recording tax is $1.50 for each $500 of face amount or fraction of it.

faqs.q: When is Jeff Davis County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 20. The usual mailing date is October 20, and partial payments are accepted up to the deadline.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Jeff Davis County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: Dial (912) 375-6622 or visit 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, in Hazlehurst. For valuation, phone the Tax Assessor at (912) 375-6624.

faqs.q: What does paying late cost in Jeff Davis County?
faqs.a: Interest each month at the bank prime rate, and 5% more every 120 days until the penalty hits 20%. A mobile home paid after April 1 owes 10% plus 1% monthly.

faqs.q: When can Jeff Davis County owners claim homestead?
faqs.a: From January 1 through April 1 for that tax year. Georgia law offers no extension.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline in Jeff Davis County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the notice. Send a letter to the Board of Tax Assessors naming the route you choose.
